data.title: Fabricated Documents Attributed to the Organisation
data.summary:
Documents presented as internal — memoranda, policies, correspondence — were circulated
as evidence for the campaign's claims. Examination indicates fabrication or alteration.
data.description:
A document outperforms an assertion. It looks like evidence, it is shareable, and it
shifts the burden onto the organisation to prove a negative about something it never
wrote.

Fabrications are rarely perfect and the defects are worth recording precisely: wrong
template revision, a logo taken from the public website rather than the document
template, job titles that did not coexist, dates that fall on weekends, and file
metadata inconsistent with the claimed author. Where the document is a genuine one that
has been altered, the alteration is the finding and the original's provenance matters.

Resist the temptation to publish a full forensic refutation. It confirms the document is
worth discussing and supplies the operator with a list of defects to correct in the next
version.
data.recommendation:
* Preserve the circulated artefact and its metadata before it is deleted; an unpreserved
  observation cannot be relied on later.
* Confirm internally whether a genuine original exists, and whether it leaked, before any
  public statement — denying a real document is the worst available outcome.
* Respond with a short provenance statement rather than a detailed forensic breakdown.
* Report the artefact to platforms under their manipulated-media policies.
data.short_recommendation: Preserve the artefact, confirm internally, respond on provenance only.
